title: The first Olympic Games had one event

sentences.text: The Olympic Games are very old.
They started in Greece.
About two thousand eight hundred years ago.
sentences.translationRu: Примерно две тысячи восемьсот лет назад.

sentences.text: Today there are many sports.
Running, swimming, jumping, boxing.
More than three hundred events.
The first games had one.
Only one.
It was a running race.
About one hundred and ninety metres.
The length of the stadium.
That was the whole games.
One race, and then everybody went home.
sentences.translationRu: Один забег — и все расходились по домам.

sentences.text: We know the name of the first winner.
He was a cook.
Slowly they added more sports.
Longer races. Then wrestling.
Then a race in armour.
Runners carried a shield and a helmet.
It was very heavy and people fell.
sentences.translationRu: Было очень тяжело, и люди падали.

sentences.text: The crowd liked that part.
There were no medals.
The winner got a crown of leaves.
From a tree near the temple.
That sounds like a small prize.
It was not.
At home his city gave him money.
sentences.translationRu: Дома его город давал ему деньги.

sentences.text: And free food for the rest of his life.
sentences.translationRu: И бесплатную еду до конца жизни.

sentences.text: Sometimes they broke the city wall.
sentences.translationRu: Иногда в стене города пробивали проход.

sentences.text: So he could enter through a new hole.
sentences.translationRu: Чтобы он вошёл через новое отверстие.

sentences.text: A city with a hero, they said,
sentences.translationRu: Город, у которого есть герой, говорили они,

sentences.text: does not need a wall.
There was one strange rule.
During the games, wars had to stop.
sentences.translationRu: На время игр войны должны были прекращаться.

sentences.text: Not everywhere, and not always.
But enough for people to travel safely.
sentences.translationRu: Но достаточно, чтобы люди могли безопасно доехать.

sentences.text: The games ran for over a thousand years.
Then they stopped for fifteen hundred.
And then somebody started them again.
sentences.translationRu: А потом кто-то начал их заново.

title: A football is not actually round

sentences.text: Look closely at a football.
It is made of flat pieces.
Sewn or glued together.
So it is not a true ball.
It is a shape with many flat sides.
sentences.translationRu: Это фигура со множеством плоских граней.

sentences.text: The classic one has thirty-two pieces.
sentences.translationRu: У классического мяча тридцать два куска.

sentences.text: Twenty white ones with six sides.
Twelve black ones with five sides.
Why not use only six-sided pieces?
Because six-sided pieces make a flat sheet.
sentences.translationRu: Потому что шестиугольники дают плоский лист.

sentences.text: Like the floor of a bathroom.
They will never curve.
The five-sided pieces are what bend it.
Each one pulls the sheet inwards.
You need exactly twelve of them.
Not eleven. Not thirteen. Twelve.
This is not a football rule.
It is a rule about shapes.
It is true for any ball made this way.
sentences.translationRu: Оно верно для любого такого мяча.

sentences.text: The black and white colours came later.
They were chosen for television.
Television was black and white then.
A plain brown ball was hard to see.
sentences.translationRu: Простой коричневый мяч было плохо видно.

sentences.text: The pattern made it easy to follow.
And you could see it spinning.
sentences.translationRu: И было видно, как он вращается.

sentences.text: Modern balls have fewer pieces.
Some have only six.
Fewer seams means a smoother surface.
And a smoother ball moves differently.
sentences.translationRu: А более гладкий мяч летит иначе.

sentences.text: One World Cup ball was very smooth.
sentences.translationRu: Один мяч чемпионата мира был очень гладким.

sentences.text: Goalkeepers complained about it for months.
It moved in the air in a strange way.
sentences.translationRu: Он странно вёл себя в воздухе.

sentences.text: Scientists tested it and agreed.
A ball that is too smooth
does not hold the air around it.
It moves late, and suddenly.
Which is exactly what a goalkeeper hates.
sentences.translationRu: А это ровно то, что вратарь ненавидит.

sentences.text: The next ball had small bumps added.
sentences.translationRu: У следующего мяча добавили мелкие бугорки.

sentences.text: On purpose, to make it less perfect.
sentences.translationRu: Нарочно, чтобы сделать его менее совершенным.

title: How a colony of ants solves a problem nobody understands

sentences.text: Put food near an ant nest and wait.
sentences.translationRu: Положи еду рядом с муравейником и подожди.

sentences.text: At first the ants wander.
They go in every direction, badly.
An hour later there is a clean line.
Two-way traffic, on the shortest route.
No ant worked this out.
sentences.translationRu: Ни один муравей этого не вычислил.

sentences.text: No ant could.
sentences.translationRu: Ни один и не смог бы.

sentences.text: An individual ant is not clever.
It has around a quarter of a million neurons.
sentences.translationRu: У него около четверти миллиона нейронов.

sentences.text: It cannot see the nest and the food at once.
sentences.translationRu: Он не видит гнездо и еду одновременно.

sentences.text: It has no map and no plan.
sentences.translationRu: У него нет ни карты, ни плана.

sentences.text: What it has is a chemical.
sentences.translationRu: Что у него есть — это вещество.

sentences.text: An ant that finds food walks home
leaving a faint trail behind it.
Other ants prefer to follow a trail.
sentences.translationRu: Другие муравьи предпочитают идти по следу.

sentences.text: And they add their own as they go.
That is the entire rule.
Follow the smell, and add to it.
sentences.translationRu: Иди по запаху и добавляй к нему.

sentences.text: Now watch what that produces.
sentences.translationRu: Теперь смотри, что из этого выходит.

sentences.text: Imagine two routes to the same food.
sentences.translationRu: Представь два пути к одной еде.

sentences.text: One short, one long.
Ants take both, at random, at first.
sentences.translationRu: Сначала муравьи идут по обоим, случайно.

sentences.text: The ones on the short route get back sooner.
sentences.translationRu: Те, кто на коротком, возвращаются раньше.

sentences.text: So they lay their trail sooner.
And they go back out and lay it again.
sentences.translationRu: Потом выходят снова и кладут его снова.

sentences.text: The short route gets stronger faster.
A stronger trail attracts more ants.
sentences.translationRu: Более сильный след притягивает больше муравьёв.

sentences.text: More ants make it stronger still.
sentences.translationRu: Больше муравьёв делают его ещё сильнее.

sentences.text: Meanwhile the chemical evaporates.
The long route fades faster than it is refreshed.
sentences.translationRu: Длинный путь выцветает быстрее, чем обновляется.

sentences.text: Within an hour it is gone.
Nobody chose the short route.
It was not compared to the long one.
It simply survived a process.
That evaporation matters more than it sounds.
Without it the first trail would win forever.
sentences.translationRu: Без него первый след побеждал бы навсегда.

sentences.text: Even after the food was gone.
Forgetting is what lets the colony change its mind.
Engineers now copy this deliberately.
It is used to route data through networks.
sentences.translationRu: Это применяют для маршрутизации данных в сетях.

sentences.text: And to plan delivery vans around a city.
sentences.translationRu: И для планирования развозки по городу.

sentences.text: The method is named after the ants.
Which is unusually honest for engineering.

title: A quarter of a country sits below the sea

sentences.text: Around a quarter of the Netherlands
lies below sea level.
More than half is at risk of flooding.
The largest cities are in that half.
sentences.translationRu: И крупнейшие города — в этой половине.

sentences.text: None of that is a natural accident.
Much of the land was under water
sentences.translationRu: Немалая часть этой земли была под водой

sentences.text: and was taken back on purpose.
The method is old and unglamorous.
Build a wall around a shallow area.
Then pump the water out from inside it.
Windmills did this for centuries.
Thousands of them, working in stages.
Each one lifting water a metre or two.
Passing it to the next one along.
The land that appears is excellent.
Flat, fertile, and immediately below the sea.
sentences.translationRu: Плоская, плодородная и сразу ниже моря.

sentences.text: Which means the pumping never stops.
sentences.translationRu: А значит, откачка не прекращается никогда.

sentences.text: Not for a season. Not for a year.
sentences.translationRu: Ни на сезон. Ни на год.

sentences.text: Stop pumping anywhere in the country
sentences.translationRu: Останови откачку где угодно в стране —

sentences.text: and the water comes back within weeks.
The whole landscape is a machine
that has been switched on since the Middle Ages.
The decisive event was in 1953.
A storm met a spring tide at night.
sentences.translationRu: Шторм совпал с высоким приливом ночью.

sentences.text: The old dykes failed in many places at once.
sentences.translationRu: Старые дамбы рухнули сразу во многих местах.

sentences.text: More than eighteen hundred people died.
The response was not to rebuild what failed.
sentences.translationRu: Ответом было не восстановить то, что рухнуло.

sentences.text: It was to ask a different question.
Not how high was the last flood.
But how often should this area flood at all.
sentences.translationRu: А «как часто этот район вообще должен затапливаться».

sentences.text: They chose numbers and then built to them.
sentences.translationRu: Выбрали числа — и строили под них.

sentences.text: Once in four thousand years for a city.
sentences.translationRu: Раз в четыре тысячи лет для города.

sentences.text: Once in a thousand for farmland.
That is a political decision, not an engineering one.
sentences.translationRu: Это политическое решение, а не инженерное.

sentences.text: It says out loud what a life is worth
sentences.translationRu: Оно вслух говорит, сколько стоит жизнь

sentences.text: compared to the cost of a wall.
Most countries never write that number down.
sentences.translationRu: Большинство стран этого числа не записывает.

sentences.text: The current thinking has changed again.
Higher walls create a quiet problem.
They make the rare failure worse.
So some dykes have been moved backwards.
Fields are allowed to flood on purpose.
Giving the water somewhere to go
turns out to beat telling it not to come.
sentences.translationRu: оказалось лучше, чем запрещать ей приходить.

title: The voice that scientists examined after it was gone

sentences.text: Most singers are described in adjectives.
Powerful, warm, distinctive, unique.
None of which can be checked.
In 2016 a group of voice scientists
decided to check one of them anyway.
sentences.translationRu: всё же решила проверить один из них.

sentences.text: They analysed recordings of Freddie Mercury.
And they hired a singer to imitate him
sentences.translationRu: И наняли певца, чтобы тот его имитировал

sentences.text: while a camera filmed inside the throat.
sentences.translationRu: пока камера снимала происходящее в горле.

sentences.text: The first finding contradicted a famous claim.
His range was often reported as four octaves.
The recordings do not support that.
What they support is something else.
He was, by the measurements, a baritone
who sang most of his work as a tenor.
sentences.translationRu: который пел большую часть своего репертуара как тенор.

sentences.text: Which is harder, and audibly so.
sentences.translationRu: Это труднее — и слышно, что труднее.

sentences.text: The effort is part of the sound.
The second finding was the interesting one.
His vibrato was irregular.
Trained classical vibrato is even.
A steady wobble, around six times a second.
sentences.translationRu: Ровное колебание, около шести раз в секунду.

sentences.text: His was faster and less regular.
sentences.translationRu: У него — быстрее и менее регулярное.

sentences.text: Which a conservatoire would call a fault.
Listeners call it emotion.
Then they found something rarer.
sentences.translationRu: А потом нашли кое-что более редкое.

sentences.text: Evidence of a second set of folds vibrating.
Structures above the vocal cords
that most people never use for sound.
sentences.translationRu: которые большинство людей для звука не использует.

sentences.text: Throat singers in Central Asia use them.
sentences.translationRu: Горловые певцы Центральной Азии их используют.

sentences.text: Very few pop singers do.
Two things vibrating at slightly different rates
sentences.translationRu: Две вибрации с чуть разной частотой

sentences.text: produce a rough, layered tone.
The word people reach for is grit.
What is worth taking from this is not the ranking.
Nobody proved he was the best at anything.
sentences.translationRu: Никто не доказал, что он в чём-то лучший.

sentences.text: What the study shows is more specific.
Several of the qualities people loved
were technically irregularities.
A voice trained out of them
sentences.translationRu: Голос, из которого их бы вытренировали,

sentences.text: would have been more correct and less recognisable.
sentences.translationRu: был бы правильнее и менее узнаваем.

sentences.text: Which is a fair description of most style.
sentences.translationRu: А это неплохое описание стиля вообще.

sentences.text: It is usually what somebody failed to remove.
sentences.translationRu: Обычно это то, что кто-то не сумел убрать.

title: Putting out every fire is what made the fires worse

sentences.text: For most of the twentieth century
forest policy in several countries was simple.
sentences.translationRu: лесная политика в ряде стран была проста.

sentences.text: Put out every fire, as fast as possible.
sentences.translationRu: Тушить каждый пожар как можно быстрее.

sentences.text: The reasoning was obvious.
Fire destroys forest. Forest is valuable.
Therefore stop the fire.
The policy worked, which was the problem.
sentences.translationRu: Политика сработала — в этом и была проблема.

sentences.text: Many forests are not damaged by fire.
They are maintained by it.
A fire passing through every decade or so
burns what is lying on the ground.
sentences.translationRu: выжигает то, что лежит на земле.

sentences.text: Dead needles, fallen branches, small shrubs.
sentences.translationRu: Сухую хвою, упавшие ветки, мелкий подлесок.

sentences.text: It moves fast and stays low.
sentences.translationRu: Он идёт быстро и держится низко.

sentences.text: Mature trees have thick bark
and their lowest branches are high up.
The fire passes underneath them.
Some species need it to reproduce.
sentences.translationRu: Некоторым видам он нужен для размножения.

sentences.text: Their cones are sealed with resin
which only melts in heat.
A forest with no fire is a forest
that is quietly filling up.
Each year adds fuel that nothing removes.
sentences.translationRu: Каждый год добавляет топливо, которое ничто не убирает.

sentences.text: Young trees grow densely in the shade.
sentences.translationRu: В тени густо растут молодые деревья.

sentences.text: They form a ladder from the ground
to the branches of the old trees.
Do that for eighty years
and the next fire is not the old kind.
sentences.translationRu: и следующий пожар будет не прежним.

sentences.text: It climbs the ladder into the crowns.
sentences.translationRu: Он забирается по лестнице в кроны.

sentences.text: And a crown fire kills everything.
Including the trees that survived the others.
So a century of successful suppression
produced forests that burn catastrophically.
Not despite the policy. Because of it.
The people who lived there knew this.
Many indigenous communities burned deliberately.
In cool seasons, in small patches, for millennia.
sentences.translationRu: В прохладный сезон, малыми участками, тысячелетиями.

sentences.text: That practice was banned in several countries
sentences.translationRu: Эту практику запретили в ряде стран

sentences.text: by the same authorities writing the policy.
sentences.translationRu: те же власти, что писали ту политику.

sentences.text: It is now being reintroduced
under the name of controlled burning.
Which is an awkward sentence
for anyone reading the dates carefully.
sentences.translationRu: для всякого, кто внимательно читает даты.

title: Nobody has agreed what time it is

sentences.text: Time feels like something measured.
A thing out there, that clocks report.
sentences.translationRu: Чем-то существующим, о чём часы сообщают.

sentences.text: It is closer to something negotiated.
For most of history the definition was the Earth.
sentences.translationRu: Большую часть истории определением была Земля.

sentences.text: One rotation is a day.
Divide it and you have the second.
This has one flaw, discovered late.
sentences.translationRu: У этого есть изъян, обнаруженный поздно.

sentences.text: The Earth is not a reliable clock.
It is slowing down, very gradually.
Mostly because the Moon is pulling on the oceans.
sentences.translationRu: В основном потому, что Луна тянет океаны.

sentences.text: And the tides drag against the seabed.
It also speeds up and slows unpredictably.
sentences.translationRu: Она ещё и непредсказуемо ускоряется и замедляется.

sentences.text: Earthquakes change it. Weather changes it.
sentences.translationRu: Землетрясения меняют её ход. Погода меняет.

sentences.text: Water moving between ice and ocean changes it.
sentences.translationRu: Вода, переходящая из льда в океан, меняет.

sentences.text: So in 1967 the second was redefined.
It is now a count of oscillations
in a particular atom under particular conditions.
A number of them, exactly, every second.
Atomic clocks are extraordinarily stable.
The best would lose under a second
over the age of the universe.
Which creates the awkward situation.
We now have two kinds of time.
sentences.translationRu: Теперь у нас два вида времени.

sentences.text: One is perfectly regular and means nothing.
sentences.translationRu: Одно идеально ровное и ничего не значит.

sentences.text: The other wobbles and decides when the sun rises.
sentences.translationRu: Другое шатается и решает, когда взойдёт солнце.

sentences.text: Civil time has to follow the second one.
Or noon slowly drifts towards the evening.
sentences.translationRu: Иначе полдень медленно уползёт к вечеру.

sentences.text: The fix was the leap second.
Occasionally a minute contains sixty-one.
sentences.translationRu: Иногда в минуте шестьдесят одна секунда.

sentences.text: Added by international decision, with months of warning.
sentences.translationRu: Добавляется международным решением, с предупреждением за месяцы.

sentences.text: Twenty-seven have been added since 1972.
Computers hated every one of them.
Software assumes minutes have sixty seconds.
sentences.translationRu: Программы считают, что в минуте шестьдесят секунд.

sentences.text: Financial systems, airlines and networks
have all failed on leap-second days.
sentences.translationRu: все падали в дни високосной секунды.

sentences.text: Some large companies now smear it instead.
Slowing their clocks fractionally across a day
sentences.translationRu: Чуть замедляя часы в течение суток,

sentences.text: so the extra second never arrives at once.
sentences.translationRu: чтобы лишняя секунда не приходила разом.

sentences.text: Which means their time is deliberately wrong.
sentences.translationRu: То есть их время нарочно неверно.

sentences.text: In a controlled and documented way.
In 2022 it was agreed to stop adding them
sentences.translationRu: В 2022 году договорились перестать их добавлять

sentences.text: by around 2035.
Letting the two times drift apart
and leaving the problem to a later generation.
Which is how most calendars have always worked.
sentences.translationRu: Так, впрочем, работали почти все календари.
